faq_heading: Pet-friendly condos in South Surrey and White Rock: your questions answered

faq.q: Which condo buildings in South Surrey and White Rock allow dogs?
faq.a: Most do. The tables on this page show, for every condo building with recent MLS® listings, whether the listings say dogs and cats are allowed and how many pets. A short list of buildings say no pets or cats only. Confirm in the bylaws before you buy.

faq.q: Can a strata in BC ban pets?
faq.a: Yes. A strata corporation can ban pets or limit their number and kind by bylaw. A pet already living in the home when a new bylaw passes can stay, and certified guide and service dogs are exempt from pet bylaws.

faq.q: How many pets are allowed in a BC strata?
faq.a: It depends on the strata's bylaws. If it has not written its own, the Province's standard bylaw allows one dog or one cat, up to two caged birds, and a reasonable number of fish or small caged animals. Many complexes allow two pets.

faq.q: Where do I find the pet bylaws before I buy?
faq.a: In the strata documents: the bylaws, the rules and the minutes, which come with the Form B. Before you remove subjects, ask the strata manager in writing whether your pet is allowed; Jared can do this for you.

faq.q: Can I rent out a condo in South Surrey and White Rock?
faq.a: Long-term, yes. Since November 24, 2022 a BC strata cannot ban or cap long-term rentals. A strata can still ban short-term stays such as Airbnb, and your tenant must follow the pet bylaws.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

These are the condos for sale in South Surrey and White Rock whose MLS® listing says pets are allowed. Limits differ by complex, so check it in the tables below, then ask me for the bylaws before you write an offer.

items.t: Pets:
"Yes, with limits" means the listings say pets are allowed with restrictions; "No" means they say no pets; "Ask me" means listings in the same complex disagree; "Not stated" means none of them say.
Dogs and Cats:
what the listings' dog and cat fields say. A dash means the listings leave them blank.
How many:
the number of pets the listings give, when they all give the same number.

blocks.text: What "pets allowed, with limits" usually means

items.t: How many:

most listings that give a number say one or two pets. The Province's standard bylaw, which applies when a strata has not written its own, allows one dog or one cat, up to two caged birds, and a reasonable number of fish or small caged animals.
What kind:
a strata can limit the kind of pet, not just the number, and some limit dogs by size or weight.
Where:
leash rules, no pets in the pool or gym, and which elevator to use are in the bylaws and rules.
Renting it out later:
